la:verb:perfero.html:
per-fĕro, tŭli, lātum, ferre, v. a.,
to bear or carry through to a certain place or end.
Lit. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): lapis nec pertulit ictum,did not bring the blow home, did not reach the mark,: hasta perlata sub papillam,: per arma pertulit ictum,: partum,to go the full time,.—Pass., ; cf.: ventrem perferre,; : Aeneas tulit patrem per ignes, et pertulit,.—
Transf.
To carry, bring, convey (class.; syn.: refero, defero): perferre mandata alicujus ad aliquem,: cum has quam primum ad te perferri litteras vellemus,: alicui nuntium alicujus rei,; ; : epistulam,.—Pass.: perferri, to be brought, conveyed to a person or place, to reach, arrive, come: cum ad eum fama tanti exercitūs perlata esset, : perfertur circa collem clamor,resounds round the hill,; ; : ad urbem terror,.—
In partic., to convey news, to announce, state, etc. (class.): et litteris multorum et sermone omnium perfertur ad me, incredibilem tuam virtutem et fortitudinem esse,I am informed,; : nuntius perfert incensas naves,; ; .—
Se, to betake one's self somewhere, to go: hinc te reginae ad limina perfer,. —
Trop.
To bear, support, or endure to the end: decem annorum poenam,: onus,: intrepidos ad fata novissima vultus,kept, maintained,: leve est miserias ferre, perferre est grave,.—
To bring to an end, to carry through, carry out; to complete, accomplish: laborem,: id quod suscepi, quoad potero, perferam,: jussa omnia,: suum imperium,i. e. to do what one bids others do,: est utique jus vetandi, cum lex feratur, quamdiu non perfertur, Cic. Cornel. Fragm. ap. Ascon.: legem pertulit, ut, etc.,carried it through, got it passed,; cf. : actionem,: causam,: rogationem,; .—
To carry out, conduct, manage (post-Aug.): patronum perferendae pro se legationis eligere,.—
In gen., to bear, suffer, put up with, brook, submit to, endure (class.; cf.: patior, sino, tolero): perfer, si me amas,: perfero et perpetior omnes,: pati, perferre, non succumbere,: frigore, et fame, et siti, ac vigiliis perferendis,: luxuriem, crudelitatem, avaritiam, superbiam,: pauperiem,: perfer et obdura,; : omnes indignitates contumeliasque,: laborem,: monstra,.—
(Like pati.) To permit, suffer; with an object-clause: excindi urbes suas seque cremari pertulerunt,: Achilles Cessare in Teucros pertulit arma sua, (8, b, 14).—
Transf., to bear the penalty of (eccl. Lat.): qui peccata nostra ipse pertulit in corpore, Pet. 2, 24.—Hence, perfĕrens, entis, P. a., bearing, brooking, patient; with gen., analog. to patiens: injuriarum,.

per-fĭcĭo, fēci, fectum, 3, v. a.
facio
,

Lit.: comitiis perficiendis undecim dies tribuit,: iis comitiis perfectis,: bellum,: aliquid absolvi et perfici,: multa,: scelus,to perpetrate,: cogitata,: instituta,: poëma,: conata,: nihil est simul et inventum et perfectum,: centum annos,to complete, live,.—So of commissions, orders, to execute: munus,; ; : jussa,: mandata,.—
Transf.
To bring to completion, finish, perfect (opp. inchoare): candelabrum perfectum e gemmis clarissimis,: murum,: loricam,: aedem,: cibos ambulatione,to digest,: cucumeres,: coria, to dress or curry, : lanas,: minium,.—
To make perfect, to perfect: aliquem citharā,: expleta et perfecta forma honestatis, Cic. Fin. 2, 15, 48: artem,.—
To bring about, to cause, effect; with ut, ; : perfice ut putem,convince me,; : eloquentia perfecit, ut, etc.,.—With ne and subj.: omnia perfecit, quae senatus salvā re publicā ne fieri possent perfecerat,. —
In mal. part., = ἐνεργεῖν, ; cf. ; .— perfectus, a, um, P. a., finished, complete, perfect, excellent, exquisite (class.).
Of persons: oratorem plenum atque perfectum esse, etc.,: homines in dicendo,: perfectis et absoluti philosophi,: homines,; : in geometriā,: in arte,.—In a religious sense, righteous (eccl. Lat.): cor perfectum,; .—Perfectissimus, a title of honor under the later emperors, Cod. Const. 12, tit. 33; Am. 21, 16 init.; .—
Of inanim. and abstr. things: naturae,: ratio,: pulchriora etiam Polycliti et iam plane perfecta (signa),: perfectum atque absolutum officium,: perfecta cumulataque virtus,: aetas, full or ripe age, the age of fiveand-twenty, init.—Comp.: valvae perfectiores,: aliquid perfectius,; ; ; : ad perfectiora,.—Sup.: quod ego summum et perfectissimum judicem,; ; ; .—Adv.: perfectē, fully, completely, perfectly (class.): eruditus,; : veritatem imitari,.—Comp., ; .—Sup.,

la:verb:perfundo.html:
per-fundo, fūdi, fūsum, 3, v. a.,
to pour over, to wet, moisten, bedew, besprinkle (class.; syn.: umecto, aspergo, imbuo).
Lit.: aquā ferventi Philodamus perfunditur,: fluviis pecus,: greges flumine,: perfusus liquidis odoribus,: postquam perfusus est, had bathed, : panis perfusus aquā frigidā,: pisces olivo,: aliquem lacrimis,; so, poet.: Aurorae lacrimis perfusus,living far in the East,: perfundi nardo,: boves hic perfunduntur,bathe themselves,; .—
Transf.
To pour into any thing (post-Aug.): sextarios musti in vas,.—
To cause to flow out, i. e. to knock out an eye (post-class.): ut oculus puero perfunderetur, dub. (al. perfodere or effundere).—
Of perspiration or of streams, to pour or flow over, to drench, bathe (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): ossaque et artus Perfundit toto proruptus corpore sudor,: tot amnium fontiumque ubertas totam Italiam perfundens,: Venafrano (oleo) piscem perfundere,.—
Of garments, to steep, dye (poet.): ostro Perfusae vestes,steeped in purple,.—
To scatter or sprinkle over, to besprinkle, bestrew (poet.): canitiem immundo perfusam pulvere turpans,: sanguine currum,: penates sanguine,: Lethaeo perfusa papavera somno,: scena perfusa croco,.—
To cover (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): omne genus perfusa coloribus,: auro tecta,: pedes amictu,.—
Of the sun's beams or fire, to flood or fill (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): sol perfundens omnia luce,; cf. : cubiculum plurimo sole perfunditur,: campos lumine (facis),.—
Trop.
To imbue, inspire, fill with any thing (class.): ad perfundendum animum tamquam illiquefactae voluptates,: sensus jucunditate quādam perfunditur,: sensus dulcedine omni quasi perfusi,: di immortales, qui me horror perfudit!: laetitiā,: gaudio,: timore,.—
In partic., to fill with the apprehension of any thing, i. e. to disturb, disquiet, alarm: nos judicio perfundere,: litora bello rapido,; cf.: (Mars) perfusus pectora tempestate belli,. —
To imbue slightly, make superficially acquainted with any thing (the fig. being borrowed from dyeing; post-Aug.): perseveret perbibere liberalia studia, non illa, quibus perfundi satis est, sed haec, quibus tingendus est animus,; cf.: acceperit: si illā (notitiā) se non perfuderit, sed infecerit,.
